text:
maria-support: FYI ACME (tenant acme-prod) reporting p95 ~450ms -> 1.8s and p99 ~2.8s on /v1/generate since 09:10 UTC. No errors, just tail latency. Customer impact: interactive chat sessions getting laggy.

acme-sre: reproducer attached — small curl load: 
```
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"short prompt","history_tokens":1024}'; done
```
Latency spikes show up after ~40-50 requests.

sam-runtime: can you paste the tenant id and a sample request id if you have one? Also checking if they moved to longer contexts or enabled prefix caching recently.

acme-sre: tenant: acme-prod. Sample request ids: req-20260317-1a2b3c, req-20260317-1a2b9f. We started rolling a longer-history change yesterday, but only to ~30% of users.

kai-sre: looking at infra metrics now — I see increased GPU mem fragmentation on host gpu-12 around 09:05 UTC. p99 queue time for that host jumped. ops-bot: auto-scale event at 09:12 UTC failed due to allocation error on pool default-gpu (insufficient contiguous slab).

ops-bot: [auto-scale] failed to allocate instance in pool default-gpu: slab_alloc_contiguous: no suitable block (needed 1.2G, max contiguous 1.0G).

aj-devex: common pattern: long-history chat increases KV and slab fragmentation. If allocator can't find contiguous blocks we see increased GC/compact cycles which stall tails. First mitigation short term: route acme-prod to a different pool with defragmented hosts or smaller-quantized model. Also lower `max_sequence` at runtime for this tenant to reduce per-request KV.

sam-runtime: added routing override to send acme-prod to backup-pool-2 (different AZ) at 09:20 UTC. Monitoring p99 now.

maria-support: customer says some improvement but tail still high for a subset of sessions (~10%).

kai-sre: we should attempt an allocator defrag probe on gpu-12 and gpu-14. Commands: 
```
# run in runtime admin container
redwood-ctl runtime metrics allocator histogram --host=gpu-12
redwood-ctl runtime admin defrag --host=gpu-12 --mode=probe
```
Probe will attempt a low-impact compaction and report freed contiguous bytes. If probe shows insufficient reclaim, full compaction will need host recycle.

acme-sre: what's risk of full compaction? We need minimal interruption.

kai-sre: full compaction can cause short (~1-3s) token-generation stalls per worker while pages are moved. We can schedule rolling compaction with draining: drain connections off one worker at a time and run compaction. That keeps visible disruptions low.

aj-devex: other mitigations: 
- set `kv_eviction_policy=LRU` and lower `kv_max_entries` for tenant to bound KV growth.
- enable `prefix_cache_ttl=30s` to avoid excessive prefix caching holding KV.
- reduce `batch_max_tokens` to avoid large allocations per request.
These are tenant-scoped config toggles we can apply immediately.

sam-runtime: applied kv_eviction_policy=LRU and kv_max_entries=6000 for acme-prod at 09:33 UTC. Also disabled aggressive prefix caching.

maria-support: ACME reports p95 down to ~320ms, p99 now ~900ms for most sessions, but a few sessions still hit >1.5s.

kai-sre: those sessions map to host gpu-14 which still has fragmented slabs. Running probe now — output: 
```
allocator.histogram: slab_64=120k slab_1g=3 free_runs=12 fragmented_bytes=1.1G contiguous_free=820M
defrag.probe: reclaimed=280M contiguous_after=1.1G
```
Looks like we can reclaim but still under 1.2G threshold for some allocation paths. Full compaction on gpu-14 recommended during low traffic window.

acme-sre: can you avoid full compaction and instead route heavy sessions away? We can't tolerate even brief extra stalls for some users.

sam-runtime: we created a temporary sticky route that redirects new long-history sessions to backup-pool-2; existing sessions are sticky to current workers, so they'll either finish or be migrated on reconnect. Also reduced `batch_max_tokens` cluster-wide for a short window to reduce allocation pressure.

aj-devex: additional note: for long-term fix we're tracking allocator improvements: splitting large slab classes, better coalescing heuristics, and async compaction to reduce pause times. But those are code changes. For now tenant-scoped config + routing + rolling compaction are the safe playbook.

maria-support: agreed. Action items: 
1) sam-runtime/ops to schedule rolling compaction on gpu-14 during 02:00-04:00 UTC maintenance window and drain workers.
2) sam-runtime to keep routing override until compaction completes.
3) devex/aj to send a config recipe for kv_eviction & prefix_cache changes to ACME support ticket so they can peer-review.
4) kai-sre to capture pprof/heap profiles from affected workers for postmortem.

kai-sre: capturing pprof now: `curl http://gpu-14:6060/debug/pprof/heap` -> saved. Will attach to ticket.

acme-sre: thank you — appreciate the quick triage. We'll monitor and report.

maria-support: leaving this thread open; will update when rolling compaction completes. :eyes:
